Flight Deck Sentry — Tester Guide

Companion app for the DJI RC Plus · version 0.4.2 · runs in the background while you fly · alerts you to manned aircraft before they get close

1. What it does (and doesn't)

Sentry watches the airspace around your drone and notifies you on the controller: a sound, a vibration, and a banner over the flight app. It does not show a map and does not deconflict for you. When it fires, you look at your map or AirSense and decide. It never takes the screen while you're flying, never installs updates while armed, and only ducks the flight app's audio for the second a tone plays.

It knows where your drone is from your organization's drone feed, and where manned aircraft are from public ADS-B (plus a local receiver if your truck has one). If the drone isn't in the feed yet (DroneSense closed, not signed in, or no mission selected), it protects the space around the controller instead.

Requirements. The controller must have an internet connection (cell or Wi-Fi) the whole flight: that is how Sentry gets your drone's position and the traffic. It only works while you are flying in DroneSense (open, signed in, mission selected); flying in any other app, your drone is not in the feed and Sentry protects the space around the controller instead. Android only (the RC Plus).

2. Install (5 minutes)

  1. On the RC Plus, open the browser and go to github.com/drobinson911/flight-deck-sentry/releases/latest/download/flight-deck-sentry.apk (tap the link if you are reading this on the controller). Allow "install unknown apps" when Android asks. (If you had a version older than 0.3.0, uninstall it first.)
  2. Open Flight Deck Sentry → Settings. Paste the fleet token (sent to you separately; never share it).
  3. This controller's aircraft: Sentry only sees your drone when DroneSense is open, you are signed in, and a mission is selected (that is what puts it in the feed). Do that, power the drone, then tap it in the "aircraft in the feed now" list, or type its serial from the registration card. This is permanent for this controller: Sentry watches this aircraft and no other.
  4. Back on the main screen tap ARM. Allow notifications and location, and accept the battery-optimisation exemption when asked. (Android's power saver freezes background apps' network and timers once the screen is off; the exemption tells Android not to do that to Sentry, so polling and alerts keep running with the screen off and DroneSense in front. Pre-flight shows red if it's missing.)
  5. Tap Pre-flight. Fix anything with a red ✗ (each line tells you how). Green all the way down = ready.
  6. Switch to your flight app. Sentry keeps running; its banners appear over the flight app.

3. The main screen

  • ARM / DISARM: Sentry only polls and alerts while armed. Disarm after landing.
  • Sources: each feed shows OK/WAIT and how old its data is. If "Drone feed" says NO TOKEN or TOKEN REJECTED, fix the token in Settings.
  • Bound to: the serial and callsign Sentry is watching. "Waiting for this controller's aircraft" means it's not in the feed yet.

4. What the alerts mean

AlertWhenWhat you do
▲ TRACK (amber)An aircraft's current track carries it through your area within 2 minutes. Popup + one sound.Open your map, find it, start planning. Banner counts down.
⚠ WARNING (red)Predicted to pass within ½ mile inside 60 s, or already inside the ½-mile ring. Sound + vibrate; repeats faster as it closes (every 20 → 12 → 6 s), softer on repeats.Act now: move perpendicular to its track (the banner's "Clear:" hint), or climb/descend as advised.
‼ COLLISION RISKPredicted miss under 500 ft sideways and 300 ft vertically within 60 s, or it will cross your altitude while within ½ mile. Continuous tone every 3 s. Cannot be dismissed.Immediate evasive action.
● PASSING / ○ CLEARIt's moving away / it's gone.Carry on.
Zone entryAn aircraft enters the TFR you're in, or a fence you set.Note it; the cadence above takes over.
Internet lost / regained · aircraft bound / lostHousekeeping, one sound each.Check the Sources panel.
Sentry only alerts for aircraft inside its rings AND inside the altitude band. Default band: surface up to 1,500 ft above your drone; adjust the ceiling in Settings to your own separation/deconfliction needs. Every alert makes a sound (advisory = one soft tone on entry, no repeats; warning and above repeat) so you don't have to be looking at the controller; "Quiet" style makes advisories banner-only. You never need to open Sentry while flying: stay in DroneSense and use the tools you're trained on. Sentry is a stop-gap until DroneSense warns about ADS-B traffic itself.

5. Banner buttons (you never need to open the app mid-flight)

  • Got it: quiets that aircraft's repeats for 60 s. It comes straight back if the aircraft escalates, turns toward you, or becomes a collision risk.
  • Ignore: quiets that aircraft until it clears your rings (same escape hatch). For the air attack ship you already know about.
  • Quiet 5 min: all traffic sounds off for 5 minutes; banners keep updating silently; Sentry says "sounds on" when it ends.
  • The small persistent notification has Disarm and Open Sentry; that's the only way into the app.

6. Settings you may want to touch

  • Rings: 3 / 1 / 0.5 nm by default. Ceiling above aircraft: 1,500 ft.
  • Cylinders: what Sentry protects around the controller when your aircraft isn't in the feed.
  • Prediction: TRACK at 120 s, WARNING at 60 s, COLLISION RISK at 60 s to closest approach. Why these defaults: we replayed one full day of real drone flights (86 flights, 3,500 drone/aircraft pairs with full ADS-B tracks) through Sentry. With a 180 s track alert it produced 150 false alarms (aircraft that turned away before the predicted pass); at 120 s that fell to 32, a 79 % reduction, while warnings still came a median 69 s before closest approach and no real conflict was missed. What adjusting does: more seconds = more time to manoeuvre but many more false alarms (predictions 3 min out are guesses); fewer seconds = fewer false alarms but less time to react. Change them if your operation needs it, and tell us what you chose.
  • Alert style: Standard / Quiet (Quiet doubles the intervals). Banner duration: 5 s.
  • Sounds & vibration: choose per level; Test plays it. If a sound is silent, pick another.
  • Every field auto-saves as you type; Enter or tapping outside closes the keyboard.

7. Try it before you fly: the demo replay

Settings → Replay: demo encounter. It replays a real recorded encounter (drone "DEMO-1" vs a Cirrus) through the live alert engine: you'll hear TRACK at −86 s, WARNING at −43 s, the closing repeats, PASSING and CLEAR. Tick "synthetic crossing" to hear COLLISION RISK. Nothing about the replay is live traffic.

8. Updating

Settings → App update shows installed vs latest and the notes; Download and install does the rest (one tap in Android's installer). Sentry checks once a day on its own and posts a quiet notification when there's a new one. It will never install while you're armed.

9. Test plan (you're the pros: try to break it)

Test it the way you'd test a radio you were going to bet on. For each item, note the time, what Sentry did, and what you saw on your own map. False alarms and misses are the most valuable thing you can send; "it worked" is second.

CheckHowPass looks like
Interference with the flight appArm Sentry, fly a normal hop with the flight app in front. Watch video, control latency, audio.No stutter, no dropped video, no audio loss beyond the tone's duration, no screen taken over.
Audibility and feelTap Test on the main screen with rotors turning and road noise. Try each level's sound in Settings.Tone heard and vibration felt at the operating position. If not, change the sound and tell us which one worked.
Silence outside the bandNote traffic you can see on your own map that is inside 3 nm but above 1,500 ft over you (airliners, high transits).Sentry stays silent for them. Any sound for high traffic is a bug (tell us the altitude).
Alert timingFor every TRACK/WARNING, stopwatch: banner time vs when you first saw the aircraft on your map, and how far out it was.TRACK about 2 min out, WARNING about 60 s out, for an aircraft pointed at you. Report the numbers.
Escalation and repeatsLet a warning run without touching it.Repeats get faster as it closes (20 → 12 → 6 s), softer than the first, stop the moment it's diverging, one PASSING, one CLEAR.
Got it / Ignore / QuietUse each once on a real alert.Silence for that aircraft (or 5 min) — and it comes back on its own if the aircraft escalates or turns toward you.
Internet lossKill the controller's data mid-flight for 2 minutes, then restore.One "Internet lost" alert, Sources show offline, one "regained", then normal. No flood.
Aircraft leaves the feedHave the drone's flight app disconnect briefly, or power-cycle after landing."Drone position lost" → "Waiting for this controller's aircraft" → re-binds by itself when it's back.
Screen off / force-closeTurn the screen off for 10 min while armed. Separately, swipe Sentry away from Recents while armed.Alerts still fire with the screen off. Force-closing disarms and shuts Sentry down (0.4.2); it does not come back until you ARM again.
Wrong or changed aircraftBind the wrong serial on purpose, then fix it in Settings.Sentry never watches another drone on its own; the fix takes effect live, no restart.
Pre-flight honestyRun Pre-flight with something deliberately wrong (no token, notifications off).The exact item shows red with a fix that works.
Battery and resourcesNote controller battery at ARM and DISARM for a 30-min flight; repeat without Sentry. (0.4.2 adds a Resources row with CPU/memory/battery-per-hour.)Report both numbers; we expect a small difference.
Two aircraft at onceWhen it happens, note which one Sentry talked about first.The closer/more severe one first; the other follows with its own banner.

Send screenshots of anything confusing along with the shared log.

Bugs, false alarms and misses are the most valuable thing you can send. Settings → Diagnostics → Share log (0.4.2) packages the last 24 hours of alerts, actions, feed health and resource numbers into a text file you can email from the controller.

If Sentry ever does anything dangerous, distracting, or simply not useful, say so plainly; that goes to the top of the list. Sentry is an aid, not a guarantee: it only sees aircraft that broadcast ADS-B (or that your local receiver hears), and it assumes they keep flying straight. See-and-avoid and your VO still come first.
